event_text: Anglo-Spanish War: Battle of Gravelines: The naval engagement ends, ending the Spanish Armada's attempt to invade England.
headline: Spanish Armada Sunk Off Scottish Coast, 1588
story: Barry settled beside Susan on the weathered stone wall, watching the remnants of the Spanish Armada struggle against the North Sea gales. 'Well, Susan, it seems Medina Sidonia's grand plan to restore Catholicism in England has come a bit unstuck.' Susan preened her feathers, eyes fixed on the distant ships. 'Rather more than a bit, Barry. With 130 ships and over 25,000 men, they were supposed to pick up the Duke of Parma's army in the Netherlands and march on London. Instead, they've been chased by the English navy, battered by storms, and are now limping back to Spain with barely half their fleet intact.' Barry snorted. 'And to think, Philip II was counting on the English Catholics to rise up in support. I suppose that's what happens when you rely on wishful thinking and outdated maps.' Susan shook her head. 'The English navy, on the other hand, has learned a thing or two from the privateers – they've developed a rather nifty tactic called "breaking the line" that's left the Spanish ships foundering in the open sea.'
regret_line: Apparently, invading a damp, unforgiving island with a proud history of rebelling against everyone wasn't the most brilliant idea.
winner_line: The shipbuilders and arms manufacturers, who got to work overtime replacing the wreckage and sparking a centuries-long naval arms race.
